<question>
With the new AV1 default in 4.2, our AV1 streams buffer and drop frames on the vela-v2. What's going on?
</question>
<tool_calls>
- codec_caps {"device": "vela-v2", "mime": "video/av01"} (ERROR)
  result: Error: device profile not found: 'vela-v2.json'. Available: atlas-a1.json, lumen-l3.json
- search_kb {"k": 3, "query": "AV1 buffering dropped frames decoder"}
  result: {"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far…
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: I can't determine it for vela-v2 because codec_caps failed (no profile for that device; only atlas-a1 and lumen-l3 exist). The knowledge base notes hardware AV1 depends on the SoC, not the Android version, and that devices decoding AV1 in software only can be too slow for high resolutions or frame rates, which is a plausible match for buffering and dropped frames after the AV1 default, but it is unconfirmed for this phone.
Next step: On a vela-v2, check which video/av01 decoders `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` lists and whether they are hardware (`isHardwareAccelerated()` on API 29+), log the decoder your player creates, and use `getVideoCapabilities()` to choose a sustainable resolution or fall back to VP9/H.264/HEVC.
Sources: [kb:av1-decoding]
</answer>

- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted

and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with
…

Software decoding of 4K60 is far beyond that limit, which explains the slideshow. The tools can't show what changed in 4.2, but if 4.2 began selecting this AV1 rendition for the device, that would be the trigger.
Next step: Check the 4.2 rendition-selection logic and make it consult CodecCapabilities (getVideoCapabilities() and isHardwareAccelerated()) before choosing AV1, so lumen-l3 falls back to an H.264/HEVC (lumen's hardware decoders) or lower-resolution rendition instead of AV1 2160p60.

</question>

  result: {"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later…
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: I can't confirm it for vela-v2: codec_caps returned an error since there is no profile for that device (only atlas-a1 and lumen-l3 are available). The knowledge base notes hardware AV1 decoding depends on the SoC and that many devices decode AV1 in software only; software decoding would explain extra battery use after 4.2's AV1 switch, but that is unverified here.
Next step: Check which video/av01 decoder vela-v2 devices actually use: log the codec name your player creates (c2.android.av1.decoder means software) and use `isHardwareAccelerated()` on API 29+ via `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)`; if there's no hardware AV1 decoder, fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC on that device.
Sources: [kb:av1-decoding]
</answer>

(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted

<question>
After switching our player to AV1 in 4.2, battery drain complaints come from vela-v2 owners watching AV1. Is it software decoding?
</question>
<tool_calls>
- codec_caps {"device": "vela-v2", "mime": "video/av01"} (ERROR)
  result: Error: device profile not found: 'vela-v2.json'. Available: atlas-a1.json, lumen-l3.json
- search_kb {"k": 3, "query": "AV1 software decoder battery drain"}
  result: {"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later…
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: I can't confirm software decoding for vela-v2: the codec_caps lookup failed because there is no profile for that device (only atlas-a1 and lumen-l3 are available), so I have no decoder data for it. The knowledge base does say hardware AV1 depends on the SoC rather than the Android version, and that many devices on recent Android still decode AV1 in software only, which is a plausible but unverified explanation for battery drain after the AV1 switch.
Next step: On a vela-v2 unit (or in your player logs from affected users), record which AV1 decoder gets created: c2.android.av1.decoder means software, and on API 29+ `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` on the entries from `MediaCodecList(REGULAR_CODECS)` for video/av01 tells you whether a hardware AV1 decoder exists at all; if there is none, fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC for that device.
Sources: [kb:av1-decoding]
</answer>

With 4.2's AV1 default, will the atlas-a1 decode av1_2160p60.mkv without dropping frames?
</question>
<tool_calls>
- codec_caps {"device": "atlas-a1", "mime": "video/av01"}
  result: {"android_api_level": 36, "decoders": [{"hardware": true, "max_fps_at_max_size": 60, "max_height": 2160, "max_width": 3840, "mime": "video/av01", "name": "c2.atlas.av1.decoder", "profiles": ["Main", "Main10"]}, {"hardware": false, "max_fps_at_max_size": 20, "max_height": 2160, "max_width": 3840, "mime": "video/av01", "name": "c2.android.av1.decoder", "profiles": ["Main"]}], "device": "atlas-a1", "display_hdr_types": ["HDR10", "HLG", "HDR10+"], "max_concurrent_hw_video_decoders": 16, "mime": "video/av01", "widevine_security_level": "L1"}
- ffprobe {"file": "av1_2160p60.mkv"}
  result: {"bit_rate": 531792, "duration_s": 0.5, "file": "av1_2160p60.mkv", "format": "matroska,webm", "streams": [{"avg_frame_rate": "60/1", "codec_name": "av1", "codec_type": "video", "height": 2160, "index": 0, "pix_fmt": "yuv420p", "profile": "Main", "start_time": "0.000000", "width": 3840}]}
- search_kb {"k": 3, "query": "AV1 4K60 dropped frames hardware decode"}
  result: {"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec an…
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: It should, provided it uses the hardware decoder: atlas-a1's c2.atlas.av1.decoder is hardware, supports Main and Main10, and is rated for 3840x2160 at 60 fps, and ffprobe shows av1_2160p60.mkv is AV1 Main, 3840x2160 at 60 fps, 8-bit. The device's software AV1 decoder (c2.android.av1.decoder) only manages 20 fps at 2160p, so frames would drop if the player ended up on that one. This is from capability data only; I haven't seen an actual playback run.
Next step: Verify on an atlas-a1 that the player instantiates c2.atlas.av1.decoder (log the codec name, or check `isHardwareAccelerated()` on API 29+) and play the clip while watching dropped-frame counts.
Sources: [tool:codec_caps] [tool:ffprobe] [kb:av1-decoding]
</answer>

<question>
With the new AV1 default in 4.2, is it safe to send 1080p60 AV1 to the vela-v2, or should we keep HEVC for it?
</question>
<tool_calls>
- codec_caps {"device": "vela-v2", "mime": "video/av01"} (ERROR)
  result: Error: device profile not found: 'vela-v2.json'. Available: atlas-a1.json, lumen-l3.json
- search_kb {"k": 3, "query": "AV1 1080p60 vs HEVC fallback"}
  result: {"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android\n\nAndroid ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10\n(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many\ndevices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow\nfor high resolutions or frame rates.\n\nChecks:\n- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.\n- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is\n  hardware backed.\n- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates\n  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: I can't determine this for vela-v2: vela-v2's device profile isn't available (only atlas-a1 and lumen-l3 exist), so I have no decoder data for it. The KB says hardware AV1 depends on the SoC and software AV1 can be too slow for high resolutions or frame rates, so HEVC is the safer choice until AV1 is verified.
Next step: Keep HEVC for vela-v2 for now; on the device check getVideoCapabilities().areSizeAndRateSupported(1920, 1080, 60) for video/av01 and isHardwareAccelerated() before enabling AV1.
Sources: [kb:av1-decoding]
</answer>

- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel"…
</tool_calls>
